comment: D’s substantially faster RMSprop recipe made it the strongest short-budget choice. Among the slower candidates, A’s deeper residual network with two LNs, then C’s normalized residual network, were favored over the shallow zero-LN models. B’s RMSprop recipe was favored over E’s low-rate AdamW recipe. K1012 supported the large progress-gap comparison; K1020 and K1066 informed the architecture ordering, although their shared-optimizer scope limits their use across these recipes. K1070 provided only weak support for B versus E because their architectures differ. The correct ordering does not establish a new general rule.
